investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC (curl, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS) against the venue's own official homepage found only schema.org Article JSON-LD (blog/interview posts), no Event/MusicEvent data. Level 2 STRUCTURAL: the response's own X-Powered-By header named 'Roadiz CMS' and its Content-Security-Policy header referenced 'theatredelaville-paris.notre-billetterie.com'; a direct, reasoned probe of api.theatredelaville-paris.com (the operator's own API subdomain, a documented Roadiz/API-Platform convention) returned a Hydra JSON-LD API entrypoint document listing '/events', '/event_dates', '/seasons', and '/taxons' collections — all public, unauthenticated, plain HTTP GET.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of https://www.theatredelaville-paris.com/fr returned 4 <script type="application/ld+json"> blocks, but every one is schema.org 'Article' (blog/interview posts under 'Théâtre sans frontières'), not Event/MusicEvent — no structured event data is exposed on the homepage itself.

The homepage's own response headers (X-Powered-By: Roadiz CMS; CSP referencing theatredelaville-paris.notre-billetterie.com) identified the platform. A direct probe of api.theatredelaville-paris.com (the operator's own separately-hosted API subdomain) returned a Hydra/API-Platform JSON-LD entrypoint document exposing public, unauthenticated '/events', '/event_dates', '/seasons', and '/taxons' collections. Querying these directly (GET /events?mainCategory=/taxons/63 for the site's own 'Musiques' taxonomy, GET /event_dates?event=/events/2449 for one specific music event) returned complete, first-party event records: title, full ISO start/end instants with explicit UTC offsets, venue/hall name, price range, and a stable per-performance resource ID — fully answering the investigation question with no further escalation needed.

venue_reference: Théâtre de la Ville — Sarah Bernhardt hall, 2 place du Châtelet, 75004 Paris, and its sister hall Théâtre des Abbesses, 31 rue des Abbesses, 75018 Paris — same operator, treated as one Venue entity for this pass (see identity.notes)

identity.notes: The retained homepage's own <title> reads 'Théâtre de la Ville, Théâtre des Abbesses - Paris' at the venue's own domain theatredelaville-paris.com, explicitly naming BOTH halls as one operator. The API's own event_dates record for a sampled event states place.name 'TDV-Sarah Bernhardt_Grande salle' (place slug 'tdv-sarah-bernhardt-grande-salle') — the API's own place-entity naming convention prefixes every place with 'TDV-' (Théâtre de la Ville), confirming both the Sarah Bernhardt hall and the Abbesses hall are modeled as places WITHIN one single operator/API instance, not two separate sources. This pass treats them as one canonical Venue entity per the task brief; no evidence was found requiring two separate Venue records.

site_classification.platform: Roadiz CMS (public-facing site) backed by a separate api.theatredelaville-paris.com API-Platform (Symfony) instance exposing a Hydra/JSON-LD REST API — NOT the same thing as embedded <script type=application/ld+json> markup on an HTML page (ingestion/json-ld/'s existing family); this is a genuine, documented, paginated JSON REST API with its own /events, /event_dates, /seasons, /taxons collections.

title.notes: The API's own /events/{id}.name field, stated directly, cross-checked identical on the /event_dates record for the same event.

start_date.notes: The API's own /event_dates/{id}.doorTime field ('2026-10-04T15:00:00+02:00'), stated directly. Naming caveat (honesty, not fabrication): the field is literally named 'doorTime', but cross-checking the SAME record's own 'arrayDates' (["2026-10-04T15:00:00+02:00"]), 'sortingDateTime' (identical value), and 'humanHours' (['15:00']) confirms this source's own 'doorTime' field is actually used as the performance start instant for this event, not a separate earlier door-opening time — this source does not appear to model door-time and performance-start as genuinely distinct concepts on this record.

time.value: 15:00+02:00 (explicit UTC offset present on the source's own field)
time.notes: Same field as start_date ('doorTime': '2026-10-04T15:00:00+02:00') — a full ISO 8601 instant with an explicit numeric UTC offset, not a floating local value.

end.notes: The API's own /event_dates/{id}.endDate field, stated directly as a full ISO 8601 instant with explicit UTC offset. Cross-checked consistent with the same record's own 'duration' field ('01:30:00') and the parent event's own 'duration' ('01:30'): 15:00 + 1h30 = 16:30. Unlike Tempodrom Berlin's own JSON-LD 'endDate' (which was found to mean 'last calendar day of a possibly multi-day run', not a performance end-time), this source's 'event_dates.endDate' is a genuine performance-end instant.

venue_location.value: TDV-Sarah Bernhardt_Grande salle (Théâtre de la Ville, Sarah Bernhardt hall)
venue_location.notes: The API's own /event_dates/{id}.place.name field, stated directly ('TDV-Sarah Bernhardt_Grande salle', slug 'tdv-sarah-bernhardt-grande-salle'). This is a distinguishing per-hall place entity within the single operator's own API — a future collector run against the Abbesses hall would see a differently-named/slugged place entity from the SAME API instance, not a separate source.

source_record_id.notes: The API's own Hydra '@id' for this specific performance-instance resource ('/event_dates/9332'), a persistent API-Platform database entity identifier — distinct from the parent production's own '/events/2449' id, which would be shared across multiple performance dates of the same production. This is the correct per-occurrence identifier (an /events id alone would not distinguish repeated performances of the same production).

event_url.notes: The API itself returns no 'url' field on the event/event_date record. The venue's own rendered HTML navigation was separately retained (ev-musiques-season-2627-links.txt) and contains the exact relative href '/fr/spectacles/saison-26-27/musiques/abdullah-miniawy-1' for this same event (matched by its own 'slug' field, 'abdullah-miniawy-1', which IS directly returned by the API). Resolving that retained relative href against the site's own known base origin (https://www.theatredelaville-paris.com, from ev-homepage) is standard, mechanical URL resolution, not inference.

derivation.rule: absolute event_url = base origin + relative href, via standard URL relative-resolution; the relative href is the site's own rendered navigation link for this exact event (matched by the API's own 'slug' field)

price.notes: The API's own /events/{id}.priceRange field, stated directly.

blockers.description: A production run must paginate the full /events?mainCategory=/taxons/63 collection (19 pages as of this investigation) and issue one further /event_dates?event=/events/{id} request per music event to obtain actual performance instances/dates — no single request returns the full upcoming music schedule at once, unlike e.g. tempodrom-berlin-01's single-page JSON-LD array. Not a blocker to activation, but material to the collector's own request-volume design (rate/backoff, and skipping cancelled=true event_dates).

A CONFIRMED public data path retained for events, event_dates, and taxons collections.

end, venue_location, event_url, and price all additionally PROVEN — a genuinely complete field set, including a real performance end-time (unlike most JSON-LD-only sources already investigated in prior trials).

recommended_family JSON_API with bespoke per-venue discovery/adapter code (ingestion/theatre-de-la-ville/), since no existing generic module in this repository models this Hydra events+event_dates split-entity shape — classified PARIS_BESPOKE.
No unresolved CRITICAL blocker (one MINOR note recorded about pagination/request volume).

The Musiques taxonomy (id 63) alone carries 279 events across this source's full history and at least 13 distinct works already listed for the current 2026-27 season (ev-musiques-season-2627-links.txt) — this is a genuine, substantive, recurring world/chamber/contemporary-music programme (Abdullah Miniawy, Ballaké Sissoko, Marja Mortensson, Jennifer Walshe/Ensemble Contrechamps, Le Sankyoku, etc.), not a generalist theatre with one incidental concert.
